# The claim responder misses claims typed with a typographic apostrophe

## Context

On #20670 a contributor commented "I’d like to take this." at 2026-11-15T19:46:05Z ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20670#issuecomment-6900232204)), and the claim responder never answered. The apostrophe in that comment is U+2019 (’), which smart-punctuation keyboards and editors type in place of `'`. The contributor was answered by hand ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20670#issuecomment-6900450829)).

## The Problem

Replayed on `dev` @ `d5530ef461` through `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs`:

| Comment | `isClaim` | `isWithdrawal` |
|---|---|---|
| `I’d like to work on this issue.` (U+2019) | false | false |
| `I'd like to work on this issue.` (ASCII) | true | false |
| `I‘d …` (U+2018), `Iʼd …` (U+02BC), `I´d …` (U+00B4) | false | false |
| `I’m working on this`, `I’ll take this` (U+2019) | false | false |
| `Sorry, I can’t work on this anymore` (U+2019) | false | false |
| `Sorry, I can't work on this anymore` (ASCII) | false | true |

A claim typed with smart punctuation gets no reply and no assignment. A withdrawal typed the same way is not read as one, so the claim it gives back keeps holding the issue.

## The Architectural Reality

- Every claim and withdrawal pattern spells the apostrophe in ASCII only: `i'?d`, `i'?m`, `i'?ll`, `can'?t`, `won'?t` (`WITHDRAWAL_PATTERNS` at `claimResponse.mjs:76`, `CLAIM_PATTERNS` at `:83`).
- `isClaim` and `isWithdrawal` both read the body through `claimText()` (`:101`), the one place a comment is prepared for matching. The workflow's own check (`.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml:399`) goes through `isClaim` as well.
- Design authority: `isClaim`'s JSDoc, "Whether a comment asks to work on the issue.", and `isWithdrawal`'s, "Whether a comment gives a claim back (…), which frees the issue for the next person." A comment typed with smart punctuation asks and gives back the same way.

## The Fix

In `claimText()`, fold the apostrophe look-alikes to `'` before matching: ’ (U+2019), ‘ (U+2018), ʼ (U+02BC), and ´ (U+00B4, typed as an apostrophe on some European layouts). One module constant carries the set; `claimText`'s JSDoc names the fold. The patterns stay unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `isClaim` is true for `I’d like to take this.`, `I’m working on this` and `I’ll take this`, and for the `I’d` sentence spelled with each of ‘ ʼ ´.
- [ ] AC-2: `isWithdrawal` is true for `Sorry, I can’t work on this anymore` and `I won’t continue with this`.
- [ ] AC-3: the fold creates no claim: `I don’t want to work on this, just a note.` and a fenced block holding `I’d like to work on this` stay false.
- [ ] AC-4: each new positive row fails on `dev` without the fold (red-proof, run alone) and passes with it; the unit suite passes.

## Out of Scope

- The backtick as an apostrophe: it is Markdown's code mark. Fold it only if a replayed real comment shows a miss.
- Other look-alikes (U+FF07, U+2032): no observed comment uses them.
- Re-answering past missed claims; the #20670 contributor was answered by hand.
- The claim-rate read of #21024, which reads claims through `isClaim` and reruns once this lands.

## Avoided Traps

- **Widening each pattern** (`i['’‘ʼ´]?d`, …): five spellings per apostrophe across two pattern lists, and every future pattern would have to remember it. One fold at the single read point covers them all and keeps #19971's guard against over-broad patterns intact, since a folded comment matches exactly what its ASCII spelling matches.
- **Folding inside `isClaim` only:** `isWithdrawal` would still miss.
